remarks.note: the physically blind can see what the leaders cannot
remarks.quote: They who, by the providence of God, are deprived of bodily sight, may yet, by the grace of God, have the eyes of their understanding so enlightened

remarks.note: the blind men's request as a model for the spiritual one
remarks.quote: Lord, that the eyes of our mind may be opened! Many are spiritually blind, and yet say they see, John ix. 41.

remarks.note: the bodily healings are a 'token' of giving sight to 'blind souls'
remarks.quote: As a token of this, he cured many of their bodily blindness

remarks.note: physical sight valued for what it does for faith
remarks.quote: Note, The Greatest comfort of bodily eyesight is its serviceableness to our faith and the interests of our souls.

remarks.locator: John 9:39 ('those who see might be made blind')
remarks.note: he says the verse is a metaphor taken from the healing
remarks.quote: This great truth he explains by a metaphor borrowed from the miracle which he had lately wrought.

remarks.note: physical first, then 'greater wonders... on men's souls'
remarks.quote: Wonders shall be wrought on men's bodies (v. 5, 6): The eyes of the blind shall be opened

remarks.note: reads the verse as both
remarks.quote: But this has special reference to Christ; for since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind till Christ did it (John ix. 32) and thereby encouraged us to hope in him for spiritual illumination.

remarks.note: reads the verse as ignorance becoming understanding only
remarks.quote: Those that were ignorant shall become intelligent, v. 18.

remarks.note: the opened eye is a picture of an enlightened heart
remarks.quote: By his Spirit in the word he presents the object; by his Spirit in the heart he prepared the organ.

remarks.note: 'blind by nature' = spiritually blind
remarks.quote: Those who by nature were blind, and those who, being under convictions of sin and wrath are quite at a loss and know not what to do with themselves

remarks.note: the blind in verse 18 may be idolaters (cf. Ps. 115:8)
remarks.quote: The verse before may be understood as spoken to the Gentile idolaters, whom he calls deaf and blind, because they worshipped gods that were so.

remarks.note: 'blind people that have eyes': eyes that work and do not see
remarks.quote: to which the prophet seems here to refer when he calls idolaters blind people that have eyes, and deaf people that have ears.

remarks.note: the promise applied to souls, with two physically blinded men as examples
remarks.quote: but by the power of his grace to give sight to them that were blind; not only the Gentile world, but every unregenerate soul, that is not only in bondage, but in blindness, like Samson and Zedekiah.

remarks.note: eyes that work but do not see
remarks.quote: They had the faculties, but in the things that belonged to their peace they had not the use of those faculties

remarks.note: he says outright that 'blind' here is spiritual
remarks.quote: blind, that is, as to spiritual and heavenly things, as the next words explain it: He cannot see far off.

remarks.note: bodily sight is no help to the soul
remarks.quote: The riches of the body will not enrich the soul; the sight of the body will not enlighten the soul

remarks.note: the eye of the understanding is better than bodily sight
remarks.quote: The clearness of the eye of the understanding is of greater use to us than bodily eye-sight.

remarks.note: a bodily blindness sent to teach him of the other kind
remarks.quote: Now Paul was thus struck with bodily blindness to make him sensible of his spiritual blindness

remarks.note: a blind prophet sees better for it
remarks.quote: blind through age, yet still blest with the visions of the Almighty, which need not bodily eyes, but are rather favoured by the want of them

remarks.note: physical blindness is a calamity; the Pharisees' kind is guilt
remarks.quote: It was not the calamity of blindness; but it was a blindness in which they were guilty

remarks.note: he separates the natural cause of blindness from the moral one
remarks.quote: There is a physical, natural reason for them.

remarks.note: he uses 'the blindness of the Gentile world' as a figure beside the physical healing
remarks.quote: Yet the leprosy of Israel and the blindness of the Gentile world are equally removed by the touch of His Hand at the cry of faith.

remarks.note: he draws a spiritual lesson from the physical healing's two stages
remarks.quote: Lastly, the confusedness of his sight, when first restored to him, surely conveyed, not only to him but to us all, both a spiritual lesson and a spiritual warning.

remarks.note: summarises the Nazareth text as healing of sin-blindness
remarks.quote: the healing which He offers to those whom sin had blinded

remarks.note: the verb is mostly spiritual; physical blindness is noun and adjective
remarks.quote: The word blind is used as a vb., as Jn 12 40, usually in the sense of ob scuring spiritual perception.

remarks.note: lists the figure's meanings and cites exactly the picture pages' texts
remarks.quote: Figuratively, blindness is used to represent want of mental perception, want of prevision, reckless ness, and incapacity to perceive moral distinctions (Isa 42 16.18.19; Mt 23 16 ff; Jn 9 39 ff).

remarks.note: the 'scales' are a figure inside a physical healing
remarks.quote: The "scales" mentioned were not material but in the restoration of his sight it seemed as if scales had fallen from his eyes.

remarks.note: names the figurative eye as its own category
remarks.quote: Figurative : The eye of the heart or mind, the organ of spiritual perception, which may be en- lightened or opened (Ps 119 IS).

remarks.note: the medical detail serves a figurative reference
remarks.quote: but the figurative reference is to the restoring of spiritual vision.

remarks.note: a reference-work statement of the figure
remarks.quote: Blindness denotes ignorance as to spiritual things (Isa. 6:10; 42:18, 19; Matt. 15:14; Eph. 4:18).

remarks.note: treats the opening promise as a Messianic sign
remarks.quote: The opening of the eyes of the blind is peculiar to the Messiah (Isa. 29:18).

remarks.note: same, from Smith's
remarks.quote: opening the eyes of the blind" is mentioned in prophecy as a peculiar attribute of the Messiah.

flagged.note: describes how a blind man walks as dark, doubtful, dangerous and unguided, and ends in a fall; bears directly on what the picture assumes, so Brian may want to read the sentence
flagged.quote: Those that walk as bad men will justly be left to walk as blind men

flagged.note: says of people who are poor and blind that they are wretched and miserable, citing Rev. 3:17, before calling them objects of compassion
flagged.quote: They that are poor and blind are wretched and miserable

flagged.note: treats the blind men's crying out as begging, a mild but real assumption
flagged.quote: followed him, as beggars do, with their incessant cries

flagged.note: says the healed man could have gone back to being blind content, having seen the Son of God
flagged.quote: How contentedly might this man have returned to his former blindness

flagged.note: calls Israel's blindness lasting, and sets Sodom and Egypt beside the unbelieving Jews
flagged.quote: Condemned sinners are struck blind, as the Sodomites and Egyptians

flagged.note: presents the cry of Matthew 27:25 as a curse entailed on the Jews and their children
flagged.quote: His blood be upon us and upon our children

flagged.note: says Jewish unbelief is inherited by succession
flagged.quote: the obstinacy and unbelief go by succession from generation to generation

flagged.note: says Israel was worse than the Gentiles
flagged.quote: They were even worse than the Gentiles themselves.

flagged.note: says the Jews who rejected Christ are still scattered, under a curse, in his own day
calls the ruins of Laodicea a monument to the wrath of Christ
flagged.quote: an awful monument of the wrath of the Lamb

flagged.note: uses Roman Catholics as the type of a church of tradition and 'church-oppressors' as the Pharisees' type
calls Samaritans poor and ignorant in passing

flagged.quote: Against this charge, rightly understood, Judaism has in vain sought to defend itself.
But perhaps the climax of blasphemous self-assertion is reached in the story

flagged.note: apology for his own account of Rabbinic purity rules, with a nod to 'blindness in part'
flagged.quote: These painful details, most reluctantly given

flagged.note: polemical summary of the Pharisees' system and the 'blind guides'
flagged.quote: The result was a system of pure externalism

flagged.note: calls the sight of diseased eyes in a Palestinian crowd 'disgusting'
flagged.quote: among the commonest and most disgusting sights

flagged.note: 'heathen nations' for the neighbours of Israel (used in an item, with a caution)
flagged.quote: A cruel custom therefore sanc- tioned among heathen nat ions
